key_insight: This paper clarifies when calibration improves mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, especially under distribution shift. The main takeaway is that calibrated experts can make MoEs more reliable, but the benefit depends on how the data distribution changes.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of understanding around when and why calibration helps MoE models, particularly when test data differs from training data. It tackles the challenge of aligning predictive probabilities with real-world accuracy under distribution shift.
method: Analyzes calibration at the level of individual experts rather than only the final ensemble output.
Studies MoE behavior under distribution shift to identify conditions where calibration improves accuracy and uncertainty estimates.
Compares calibrated and uncalibrated expert predictions to understand their effect on routing, aggregation, and overall model performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides guidance on when to invest in calibration for MoE systems to improve trustworthiness and robustness. It is especially useful for applications where reliable uncertainty estimates matter under changing data conditions.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing experts, gating/routing, and final MoE predictions.
A calibration curve comparing predicted confidence vs. empirical accuracy.
A before/after chart illustrating performance under in-distribution vs. shifted data.
An icon-based flow showing distribution shift and its effect on expert reliability.
paper_title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
paper_authors: Gina Wong, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Anqi Liu
